Hi Marissa / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the demo was helpful. Before we move to internal procurement, two quick commercial questions on the private (VPC) offer so we can budget correctly:

1) Platform fee proration: If we start in mid-quarter and ramp usage over the first 60 days, can the platform fee be prorated on a daily basis or do you bill whole-month platform fees? Our finance team prefers monthly invoices that reflect actual start dates.

2) Usage thresholds and credits: We expect bursty traffic in Q4. Do you provide automatic credits or tiered unit pricing once we exceed committed token thresholds? If we agree an annual commit (say X tokens/year), would that allow us to apply overage discounts or retroactive credits?

If it helps, procurement asked for: a sample invoice showing platform fee proration, and a short SOW we can route for redlines.

Appreciate a short note — we’re trying to decide between a 12- vs 24-month commitment and need the billing mechanics to compare TCO.

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by proposed options.

Short answers:
- Platform fee: we can prorate a platform fee on a daily basis for the first invoice when a deployment goes live mid-billing-cycle. Ongoing invoices are monthly.
- Usage thresholds: we support tiered per-token pricing tied to committed volumes. Overages can be handled either as per-token overage rates or converted into retroactive credits if you hit the next tier threshold within the same billing period.

Options to consider (we’ll tailor these in the SOW):
1) Monthly pro-rata platform fee then annual true-up: initial invoice is prorated daily; we do an annual true-up against committed tokens and issue credits if you exceeded commitment discounts. This is our default for 12-month terms.

2) Annual prepay with staged credits: you prepay the platform fee for the year at a discounted rate (we can bake in a 7% discount for annual prepay). If you exceed your committed tier by >20% we issue overage credits on the following quarter’s invoice.

3) 24-month commit: larger discount on platform fee (typically 10–12%) and automatic upgrade to higher reserved support tier at no additional onboarding charge. We also offer a one-time implementation credit to offset migration costs — typically expressed as a dollar credit applied to future invoices (not cash-back).

Attached: Draft_SOW_v1.3.pdf and Price_Sheet_Private_Deploy.xlsx — the SOW has the billing language and an example invoice template (bottom of page 2).

If you want a worked example with your expected token curve, send over a rough monthly estimate and I’ll model 12 vs 24 months with proration and credits so you can see net cash flows.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Draft_SOW_v1.3.pdf (PDF))

Looping in a quick finance + procurement playbook from our side. TL;DR: agreement that Marissa outlined is standard and keeps billing predictable for both sides. A few practical notes: 

- We normally issue the prorated platform fee as a separate line on the first invoice so procurement sees a clean start date and the platform fee is not amortized into usage lines.
- For annual commits where the customer requests retroactive credits, we prefer credits applied to future invoices (credit memos). If procurement needs a sample invoice, use the template in the SOW — it shows a prorated platform fee line and a quarterly true-up note.
- For the 24-month ask (10% discount), we can support that provided ClearSky agrees to minimum annual committed tokens and a baseline support tier (Standard -> Premium). Recommend adding a clause that any onboarding credits are earned only after go-live acceptance.
